new.title: Climb the Frauenkirche dome for the Old Town view
new.desc: The Baroque Frauenkirche was destroyed in the 1945 bombing and rebuilt, with the reconstruction finished in 2005. The gold cross on top was a gift from Coventry, and the dome can be climbed for views over the Altstadt and the Elbe.
new.tip: The dome climb costs about 12 EUR. Go early or at sunset to avoid queues.
new.q: Frauenkirche, An der Frauenkirche, Altstadt, Dresden

new.title: See Raphael's Sistine Madonna in the Zwinger
new.desc: The Zwinger is a Baroque courtyard palace whose free courtyard is Dresden's best-known architectural ensemble. The Gemaeldegalerie Alte Meister inside holds about 700 European works, including Raphael's Sistine Madonna.
new.tip: The courtyard is free; museums need tickets. Allow 2 hours for the Old Masters gallery.
new.q: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Theaterplatz 1, Zwinger, Dresden

new.title: Admire the treasures of the Green Vault
new.desc: The Historic Green Vault in the Residenzschloss is a Baroque treasury of goldsmith work and jewels assembled by Augustus the Strong. The Residenzschloss was rebuilt after 1945 and also houses the Armoury with its Turkish Chamber.
new.tip: Historic Green Vault entry is by timed ticket with limited numbers, so book ahead.
new.q: Residenzschloss Historisches Grünes Gewölbe, Taschenberg 2, Dresden

new.title: See Caspar David Friedrich at the Albertinum
new.desc: The Albertinum is a former arsenal converted into a museum on the Bruehl Terrace. It houses the Galerie Neue Meister, including works by Caspar David Friedrich, and the sculpture collection.
new.tip: A combined ticket with the Kunsthalle im Lipsius-Bau is available.

new.title: Walk along the Fürstenzug porcelain mural
new.desc: The Fürstenzug is a procession of Saxon rulers on horseback, shown on about 25,000 Meissen porcelain tiles over a wall 102 m long. It runs along Augustusstrasse beside the Stallhof.
new.tip: Free and always visible; best in morning light when the tiles shine.

new.title: Stroll Brühl's Terrace, the Balcony of Europe
new.desc: The Bruehlsche Terrasse is an elevated riverside promenade about 20 m above the Elbe, open to the public since 1814. It is nicknamed the Balcony of Europe and links the Albertinum, Kunstakademie and the Augustus Bridge.
new.tip: Free. Walk it at dusk, then go down to the Elbe steamer pier.

new.title: Explore the Kunsthofpassage courtyards
new.desc: The Kunsthofpassage in the Aeussere Neustadt links Alaunstrasse 70 with Goerlitzer Strasse 21-25 through a network of themed courtyards. The courtyards hold small shops, galleries, cafés and bars.
new.tip: Enter from Alaunstrasse 70. The courtyard of the elements has the famous musical drainpipes that play in the rain.
new.q: Kunsthofpassage, Görlitzer Straße 21, Äußere Neustadt, Dresden

new.title: Marvel at the tiled Pfunds Molkerei
new.desc: Pfunds Molkerei on Bautzner Strasse is a dairy shop lined with about 3,500 hand-painted Art Nouveau tiles by Villeroy & Boch. It was listed in the Guinness Book of Records in 1997 as the most beautiful dairy shop in the world.
new.tip: Buy Saxon cheese or sample the milk products; the upstairs restaurant is cash only.

new.title: Cross the Blaues Wunder bridge in Loschwitz
new.desc: The Loschwitz Bridge, nicknamed the Blue Wonder, opened in 1893 and is a steel bridge without river piers. It joins Blasewitz and Loschwitz and has a blue-green tinge that gave it its nickname.
new.tip: Walk across and have coffee or a beer on the Loschwitz side.

new.title: Wander the gardens of Pillnitz Palace
new.desc: Pillnitz Castle was the summer residence of the Saxon court, built in an Asian-inspired Baroque style on the Elbe. Its park contains a camellia tree more than 200 years old.
new.tip: Park entry is free per the Wikivoyage listing. Arrive by steamer from Dresden.

new.title: See the Yenidze, the tobacco mosque
new.desc: The Yenidze is a former cigarette factory built in the style of an Ottoman mosque, with a glass dome. It now houses offices and a dome restaurant with a rooftop beer garden.
new.tip: Go for the roof terrace view over the Altstadt at sunset.

new.title: Visit the Military History Museum and its Libeskind wedge
new.desc: The Militärhistorisches Museum der Bundeswehr in the Albertstadt is Germany's largest military history museum, with about 1.2 million objects. A steel and glass wedge by Daniel Libeskind cuts through the old arsenal building.
new.tip: Take the Libeskind wedge viewing platform for views of Dresden.
new.q: Militärhistorisches Museum der Bundeswehr, Olbrichtplatz 2, Dresden

new.title: Spend a morning at the German Hygiene Museum
new.desc: The Deutsches Hygiene-Museum covers the human body, health, culture and society, and also addresses the eugenics history of the institution. It is known for the Transparent Man model.
new.tip: Allow two to three hours. Next door is the Grosser Garten.

new.title: Stroll the Großer Garten and its park railway
new.desc: The Grosser Garten is Dresden's largest park, with the Palais im Grossen Garten and the zoo. A seasonal miniature railway runs through it, and Carolasee has rowing boats.
new.tip: Rent a bike or rollerblades for the long main avenue.

new.title: Step inside a 360-degree panorama at the Panometer
new.desc: The Dresden Panometer is housed in a former gasometer in the Reick district. It shows large 360-degree panorama paintings in the round gasworks hall.
new.tip: Check which panorama is on and book a ticket online.

new.title: Hear the Silbermann organ in the Hofkirche
new.desc: The Katholische Hofkirche on Theaterplatz is a late Baroque cathedral from 1751. It contains a Silbermann organ, and its crypt holds the tombs of Saxon rulers.
new.tip: Crypt visits are by guided tour only.

new.title: Climb the tower of the Kreuzkirche
new.desc: The Kreuzkirche on the Altmarkt is the home church of the Kruzianer boys' choir. Its tower is 92 m high.
new.tip: Check the Kreuzchor performance schedule, usually Saturday vespers.
new.q: Kreuzkirche, An der Kreuzkirche, Altmarkt, Dresden

new.title: Descend into the Dresden fortress casemates
new.desc: Beneath the Bruehl Terrace lie the remains of the old Dresden fortress, the Kasematten. A guided tour leads through the vaulted passages.
new.tip: The tour is about 4 EUR per the travel guide; entrance near the Terrace steps.

new.title: Visit the Festspielhaus in Garden City Hellerau
new.desc: The Festspielhaus Hellerau was built in 1911 to a design by Heinrich Tessenow and became a centre of modern dance. It sits in Gartenstadt Hellerau, a garden city founded in 1909 with many listed houses.
new.tip: Combine a performance with a walk through the garden city.

new.title: Climb the Hausmannsturm of the Residenzschloss
new.desc: The Hausmannsturm is a 100 m tower of the Residenzschloss with a viewing platform at 68 m. It overlooks the Zwinger, Semperoper and the Elbe.
new.tip: Best in clear weather; entrance via the palace courtyard.

new.title: Take in an opera or ballet at the Semperoper
new.desc: The Semperoper is the home of the Saxon State Opera and the Staatskapelle Dresden, founded in 1548. The building was rebuilt in 1977-85.
new.tip: Book months ahead; guided tours of the house run on most days.

new.title: Ride the Loschwitz suspension railway
new.desc: The Dresden Schwebebahn is a historic suspension railway linking Loschwitz with Oberloschwitz on the hillside. It opened in 1901 and is one of the oldest of its kind.
new.tip: Combine it with the nearby funicular and the walk down to the Blue Wonder.
new.q: Schwebebahn Dresden, Pillnitzer Landstraße, Loschwitz, Dresden

new.title: Take a paddle steamer from Dresden to Pillnitz
new.desc: The Saechsische Dampfschiffahrt runs the world's oldest and largest fleet of historic paddle steamers. Boats leave from the Terrassenufer pier and sail upriver to Pillnitz Palace.
new.tip: The Terrassenufer to Pillnitz fare was around 21 EUR for adults; check the current timetable.

new.title: Cycle the Elbe meadows on the Elberadweg
new.desc: The 1,220 km Elbe Cycle Route passes through Dresden along the riverside meadows. The wide Elbwiesen beneath the Altstadt are used for sport and picnics.
new.tip: Rent a bike in the centre and cycle toward Pillnitz or Radebeul.

new.title: Watch a film at the Filmnächte am Elbufer
new.desc: The Filmnaechte am Elbufer is an open-air cinema and concert series on the Elbe bank at Koenigsufer from June to August. The screen faces the Altstadt skyline.
new.tip: Bring a cushion and a jacket; check programme and tickets online.

new.title: Drink Glühwein at the Striezelmarkt
new.desc: The Striezelmarkt on the Altmarkt is one of Germany's oldest Christmas markets, dating back to 1434. It is known for the Dresden Stollen and the giant Christmas pyramid.
new.tip: Try Stollen from a stall carrying the Dresden Stollen seal.

new.title: Join the Bunte Republik Neustadt street festival
new.desc: The Bunte Republik Neustadt is a June street festival across the Aeussere Neustadt with stages, food stalls and courtyard parties. It started in 1990.
new.tip: Come on the Saturday evening and explore the courtyards.
new.q: Bunte Republik Neustadt, Alaunstraße, Äußere Neustadt, Dresden

new.title: Cheer on Dynamo Dresden at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion
new.desc: SG Dynamo Dresden is the city's football club, playing in a stadium with about 32,000 seats. The stadium also houses a football museum.
new.tip: Tickets are sold online; the atmosphere in the standing blocks is famous.

new.title: Hear live jazz at the Blue Note
new.desc: The Blue Note on Goerlitzer Strasse is a long-running jazz bar in the Aeussere Neustadt. It hosts live concerts and jam sessions.
new.tip: Check the concert calendar; sessions start late.
new.q: Blue Note, Görlitzer Straße 2b, Äußere Neustadt, Dresden

new.title: Skate the Friday Roller Blade Night
new.desc: The Dresden Roller Blade Night is a free group skate through the city on Friday evenings from April to September. It starts at Lingnerallee near the Hygiene Museum.
new.tip: Bring your own skates and a helmet.

new.title: Tour the Gläserne Manufaktur
new.desc: The Transparent Factory is a former Volkswagen plant with a glass facade near the Grosser Garten. One-hour guided tours show the factory and visitors can test-drive electric VWs.
new.tip: The tour cost about 5 EUR; check tour times online.

new.title: Attend a Dresden Philharmonic concert
new.desc: The Dresden Philharmonic, founded in 1870, plays in the Kulturpalast concert hall, a 1969 building rebuilt as a modern concert hall. The building also houses the central library and a cabaret.
new.tip: Choose a seat behind the orchestra for a cheaper ticket.

new.title: Swim at the Georg-Arnhold-Bad
new.desc: The Georg-Arnhold-Bad is a public pool near the Grosser Garten. It has a 93 m tube slide, a solar-heated outdoor pool and a sauna area.
new.tip: Visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds.

new.title: Party at the Hechtfest street festival
new.desc: The Hechtfest is a three-day August street festival in the Hechtviertel of the Neustadt. It has an alternative, neighbourhood feel with music and stalls.
new.tip: Wander the side streets for the smaller stages.

new.title: Eat Eierschecke at the Dresdner Kaffeestübchen
new.desc: The Dresdner Kaffeestübchen is a small café near the Frauenkirche, often named as a top spot for Eierschecke, the Dresden egg custard cake. Prinz.de recommends the Dresdner Gedeck pairing the cake with coffee liqueur.
new.tip: Order the Eierschecke with coffee; seating is small so go off-peak.

new.title: Try Eierschecke at Café Wippler by the Blue Wonder
new.desc: Café Wippler is a Loschwitz bakery-café across the Blaues Wunder bridge. Merian recommends it for a traditional Eierschecke, and a guide credits it with a tradition of more than 100 years.
new.tip: Have the Eierschecke with coffee, then walk to the bridge.

new.title: Feast at the Sophienkeller in the Taschenbergpalais
new.desc: The Sophienkeller is a vaulted cellar restaurant opposite the Zwinger, themed around Augustus the Strong. It serves hearty Saxon dishes; it was renovated after the 2002 flood.
new.tip: Mains cost about 12-20 EUR; try the Saxon roast or schnitzel.

new.title: Drink Watzke beer at the Ball- und Brauhaus
new.desc: Watzkes Ball- und Brauhaus in Pieschen is a late-19th-century brewery with a ballroom and an Elbe-view beer garden. It brews its own beer and holds themed evenings.
new.tip: Try the schnitzel and the house beer in the garden.
new.q: Ball- und Brauhaus Watzke, Kötzschenbroder Straße 1, Dresden

new.title: Dine at Raskolnikoff in the Neustadt
new.desc: Raskolnikoff opened after reunification as a bar and became a restaurant focused on seasonal produce from small regional producers. It has a garden with a fountain and is open daily.
new.tip: Sunday opens at 09:00 for breakfast.
new.q: Raskolnikoff, Böhmische Straße 34, Äußere Neustadt, Dresden

new.title: Have a beer at the Planwirtschaft pub
new.desc: Planwirtschaft on Louisenstrasse is one of the oldest pubs in the Neustadt, dating from the reunification period. It opens at 07:30 and serves draught beer and food.
new.tip: Open daily from 07:30 to 01:00.

new.title: Eat Indian food in the garden of Die Scheune
new.desc: Die Scheune on Alaunstrasse is a cultural centre with concerts, discos and readings. Its garden runs as a food and drink venue in summer, serving Indian food.
new.tip: Best on a summer evening; check for concerts in the hall.
new.q: Die Scheune, Alaunstraße 36-40, Äußere Neustadt, Dresden

new.title: Eat schnitzel at the SchillerGarten by the Elbe
new.desc: The SchillerGarten at Schillerplatz is a large beer garden by the Elbe near the Blaues Wunder. It is known for schnitzel.
new.tip: Go on a summer afternoon for the river view.

new.title: Drink in the Elbegarten Demnitz beer garden
new.desc: Elbegarten Demnitz is a large beer garden by the Blaues Wunder with live music. It is on Friedrich-Wieck-Strasse in Loschwitz.
new.tip: Come for live music on summer weekends.

new.title: Taste brewery food at the Brauhaus am Waldschlößchen
new.desc: The Brauhaus am Waldschloesschen is a hilltop brewery restaurant serving traditional German food with its own beer. It is known for a Monday pork knuckle deal.
new.tip: Try the pork knuckle and the house beer.
new.q: Brauhaus am Waldschlößchen, Am Brauhaus 8b, Dresden

new.title: Dine under the dome of the Yenidze
new.desc: The Kuppelrestaurant in the Yenidze serves food in the glass dome of the former cigarette factory. A rooftop beer garden looks over the Baroque Altstadt.
new.tip: Open daily from 11:00; book for sunset.

new.title: Grab a currywurst at Curry am Schloss
new.desc: Curry am Schloss is a tiny stand on Schlossstrasse opposite the Residenzschloss, claiming the best currywurst in town. It also serves breaded cauliflower.
new.tip: Cheap street-food stop between museums.

new.title: Sip drinking chocolate at Camondas Schokoladen-Kontor
new.desc: Camondas Schokoladen-Kontor on Schlossstrasse is a chocolate shop with a small café opposite the Residenzschloss. It serves drinking chocolate and cakes and has a chocolate museum.
new.tip: Order the hot chocolate after the Green Vault.

new.title: Eat a loaded kumpir at Keké
new.desc: Keké on Louisenstrasse serves kumpir, the Turkish baked potato, in the Aeussere Neustadt. The travel guide notes a vegetarian version for about 4.60 EUR.
new.tip: Cheap and filling for a Neustadt night out.
new.q: Keké Kumpir, Louisenstraße 21, Äußere Neustadt, Dresden

new.title: Try Thai street food at Hot Shüzzle
new.desc: Hot Shuezzle on Rothenburger Strasse serves Thai street food cooked by a chef from Thailand. It is a small Neustadt place.
new.tip: Order a curry or noodle dish at lunch.
